question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (AMD)

calls.reasoning: Q3 non-GAAP EPS consensus ~$1.93-1.94 on ~$13.06B revenue (guide $13B±0.3B, 56% non-GAAP GM); AMD typically beats modestly (~$1.97 → ~$3.28B non-GAAP net). Recent quarters show non-GAAP-to-GAAP net gap ex-investment-gains of ~$0.88-0.95B (SBC ~$0.5B, intangibles amortization ~$0.54B, tax offset), implying GAAP ~$2.3B / 1.665B shares ≈ $1.38. Q2 GAAP $1.38 was inflated by $483M investment gains; Q3 likely carries a mark-down because SpaceX (AMD's largest public stake, ~$566M) fell from a ~$225 mid-June peak to ~$151 on Sept 30, so median shaded to ~$1.36. Main uncertainty: mark-to-market on ~$1.3-1.5B equity holdings, tax discretes. Small tail below $1.00 for a large impairment or legal charge. No prediction market found (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, bookmakers).

calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on core facts (Q2 GAAP $1.38 with $483M gains, consensus ~$1.94, recurring gap ~$0.53-0.59). The factual dispute was which holding drives the Q3 mark: Run 1's 13F lists SpaceX (~$566M) as the largest public stake, while Runs 2-3 focused on Cerebras. The 13F does not list Cerebras, so SpaceX likely dominates, but the Jun 30 SpaceX price was not found and Cerebras exposure could not be ruled out. Both stocks look flat-to-down over AMD's fiscal Q3 (ended ~Sep 26), implying a small loss. Neither claim could be fully settled; I treat the mark as a -$0.00 to -$0.06 drag with symmetric uncertainty. Gap size and beat size are judgment calls; I take a typical beat and a mid-range gap, giving a median of $1.40. I carry forward a dispersion width similar to the runs' 0.35-0.42.
